_help: College minors for step 6 and the /college-minors/ pages. Majors suggest minors in majors.json (with a reason for each pairing); this file describes each minor. complements: how the minor adds to a major in general. careers: CEI career slugs the minor points toward (they count in training recommendations at the 'minor' weight). interests: interest slugs.

minors.name: Accounting
minors.summary: Adds the ability to read, prepare and analyze financial records.
minors.complements: Every organization runs on budgets and financial statements. An accounting minor helps business, healthcare, engineering and nonprofit majors understand the numbers behind decisions and manage budgets with confidence.

minors.name: American Sign Language
minors.summary: Builds communication skills with Deaf and hard-of-hearing people.
minors.complements: ASL helps education, healthcare, social work and public service majors serve Deaf and hard-of-hearing students, patients and clients, and it can be a first step toward interpreting.

minors.name: Artificial Intelligence
minors.summary: Introduces machine learning and how AI systems are built and used.
minors.complements: An AI minor helps computer science, data, engineering and business majors understand how machine learning works, where it fails, and how to apply it responsibly in their field.

minors.name: Biology
minors.summary: Adds a foundation in living systems, cells, genetics and ecology.
minors.complements: Biology supports health, environmental, engineering and chemistry majors and covers prerequisites for many health professional programs.

minors.name: Business
minors.summary: Adds core knowledge of management, finance, marketing and operations.
minors.complements: A business minor is one of the most useful additions to almost any major. It helps engineers, nurses, artists, scientists and tradespeople understand budgets, customers and management, and it prepares you to lead a team or start your own business.

minors.name: Chemistry
minors.summary: Adds lab skills and an understanding of substances and reactions.
minors.complements: Chemistry supports biology, health, nutrition, forensic, environmental and engineering majors, and it satisfies prerequisites for many health and science graduate programs.

minors.name: Communications
minors.summary: Strengthens writing, speaking and presentation skills.
minors.complements: Employers in every field ask for strong communication. A communications minor helps technical, business and science majors write clearly, present with confidence and work well on teams.

minors.name: Computer Science
minors.summary: Adds programming and computational problem-solving skills.
minors.complements: Programming is useful far beyond software jobs. A computer science minor helps math, science, engineering, business and design majors automate work, analyze data and build tools.

minors.name: Construction Management
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of how construction projects are planned, priced and built.
minors.complements: A construction management minor helps engineering, architecture, business, real estate and safety majors understand estimating, scheduling and the realities of the job site.

minors.name: Criminal Justice
minors.summary: Adds an understanding of law enforcement, courts and corrections.
minors.complements: Criminal justice pairs well with psychology, sociology, cybersecurity, forensic science and social work for careers that intersect with the justice system.

minors.name: Cybersecurity
minors.summary: Adds skills in protecting systems, networks and data.
minors.complements: Security matters in every technical role. A cybersecurity minor helps computer science, IT, information systems and criminal justice majors build secure systems and respond to threats.

minors.name: Data Analytics
minors.summary: Adds skills in collecting, analyzing and presenting data.
minors.complements: Data skills are in demand in business, healthcare, marketing, logistics and government. A data analytics minor helps you base decisions on evidence and present results clearly.

minors.name: Digital Media
minors.summary: Adds video, audio, photography and social media production skills.
minors.complements: Digital media skills help communications, marketing, journalism, music and business majors create content for websites, social media and campaigns.

minors.name: Economics
minors.summary: Adds an understanding of markets, incentives and economic policy.
minors.complements: Economics strengthens finance, business, political science, public administration and international business majors with analytical tools for markets and policy.

minors.name: Education
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of how people learn and how to teach.
minors.complements: An education minor helps subject majors such as math, science, history, art and music explore teaching, tutoring and training careers.

minors.name: Emergency Management
minors.summary: Adds disaster planning, response and recovery skills.
minors.complements: Emergency management fits fire science, EMS, public health, public administration and safety majors who want to lead preparedness and response.

minors.name: Environmental Studies
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of environmental issues, policy and sustainability.
minors.complements: Environmental studies helps engineering, biology, public health, business and safety majors understand environmental regulations and sustainability.

minors.name: Philosophy and Ethics
minors.summary: Builds skills in reasoning, argument and ethical decision-making.
minors.complements: Ethics helps AI, healthcare, business, law and engineering majors think through hard questions about fairness, privacy, safety and responsibility.

minors.name: Exercise Science
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of fitness, movement and physical health.
minors.complements: Exercise science fits health sciences, nutrition, sport management and kinesiology-related careers in wellness, coaching and rehabilitation.

minors.name: Finance
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of investments, financial markets and corporate finance.
minors.complements: A finance minor helps accounting, economics, supply chain, real estate and engineering majors understand investment decisions, cash flow and financial risk.

minors.name: Gerontology
minors.summary: Focuses on aging and the needs of older adults.
minors.complements: Gerontology helps nursing, social work, respiratory therapy and human services majors care for older adults, a large and growing population.

minors.name: Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
minors.summary: Adds mapping and spatial data analysis skills.
minors.complements: GIS is used in civil engineering, environmental science, forestry, emergency management, urban planning and public health to map and analyze location data.

minors.name: Graphic Design
minors.summary: Adds visual design, layout and design software skills.
minors.complements: Graphic design helps marketing, communications, web development and business majors create professional visuals for brands, campaigns and products.

minors.name: Healthcare Administration
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of how health organizations are managed and financed.
minors.complements: Healthcare administration helps nursing, medical assisting, public health and allied health majors move into supervisory and management roles.

minors.name: Hospitality Management
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of hotel, restaurant and guest service operations.
minors.complements: Hospitality management helps culinary, nutrition, business and tourism majors run restaurants, hotels and food service operations.

minors.name: Human Resources
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of hiring, training, pay and employee relations.
minors.complements: Human resources helps psychology, management, operations and healthcare administration majors manage people and understand employment law.

minors.name: Information Systems
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of how organizations use databases and business software.
minors.complements: Information systems helps accounting, business and healthcare majors work with the software and data that run organizations.

minors.name: Information Technology
minors.summary: Adds practical skills in networks, systems and user support.
minors.complements: IT helps health information, project management and business majors support the systems their organizations depend on.

minors.name: Legal Studies
minors.summary: Adds an understanding of law, contracts and the legal system.
minors.complements: Legal studies helps business, accounting, HR, cybersecurity, political science and real estate majors handle contracts, compliance and regulation.

minors.name: Management
minors.summary: Adds leadership, supervision and organizational skills.
minors.complements: Management helps logistics, technical and healthcare majors prepare to supervise teams and run departments.

minors.name: Marketing
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of customers, branding, promotion and digital marketing.
minors.complements: Marketing helps business, communications, design, hospitality, entrepreneurship and technical majors understand customers and promote products, services and ideas.

minors.name: Mathematics
minors.summary: Adds advanced math and quantitative reasoning.
minors.complements: Math strengthens computer science, engineering, physics, economics, finance and AI majors, and it prepares education majors to teach math.

minors.name: Nutrition
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of food, diet and health.
minors.complements: Nutrition fits exercise science, nursing, culinary arts and public health majors who want to support healthier eating.

minors.name: Occupational Safety
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of workplace hazards, OSHA rules and safety programs.
minors.complements: Safety knowledge is valued in construction, manufacturing, logistics, energy, engineering and environmental careers. A safety minor helps you protect coworkers and prepares you for safety lead and compliance roles alongside your main job.

minors.name: Physics
minors.summary: Adds a deeper understanding of matter, energy and motion.
minors.complements: Physics supports engineering, aerospace, radiologic technology and mathematics majors with the science behind their equipment and systems.

minors.name: Political Science
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of government, policy and politics.
minors.complements: Political science helps journalism, economics, history, legal studies and public relations majors understand how policy is made.

minors.name: Professional Writing
minors.summary: Builds clear, practical writing for work.
minors.complements: Professional writing helps history, digital media, science and technical majors write reports, proposals, documentation and web content.

minors.name: Project Management
minors.summary: Adds methods for planning, scheduling and delivering projects.
minors.complements: Project management helps business, construction, IT, engineering and events majors deliver work on time and on budget.

minors.name: Psychology
minors.summary: Adds an understanding of how people think, feel and behave.
minors.complements: Psychology is one of the most popular minors because it applies everywhere people are: healthcare, education, business, marketing, criminal justice and design.

minors.name: Public Health
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of disease prevention and community health.
minors.complements: Public health helps nursing, biology, health sciences, social work and emergency management majors see health at the community level.

minors.name: Public Relations
minors.summary: Adds skills in reputation, media relations and persuasive communication.
minors.complements: Public relations helps business, political science and nonprofit-minded majors manage communication with the public and the media.

minors.name: Renewable Energy
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of solar, wind, storage and clean energy systems.
minors.complements: A renewable energy minor helps electrical technology, engineering and business majors move into the growing clean energy field.

minors.name: Professional Sales
minors.summary: Adds selling, negotiation and client relationship skills.
minors.complements: Sales skills help real estate, marketing, engineering and business majors win clients and grow revenue.

minors.name: Sociology
minors.summary: Adds an understanding of groups, institutions and social issues.
minors.complements: Sociology helps public health, psychology, criminal justice and social work majors understand the social forces that shape people's lives.

minors.name: Spanish
minors.summary: Builds the ability to communicate in Spanish.
minors.complements: Spanish is the most widely spoken language in the U.S. after English. A Spanish minor helps healthcare, education, social work, criminal justice, hospitality and business majors serve more people.

minors.name: Special Education
minors.summary: Adds strategies for teaching and supporting students with disabilities.
minors.complements: A special education minor helps elementary and secondary education majors support every learner and can broaden licensure options in some states.

minors.name: Statistics
minors.summary: Adds the tools to collect, analyze and interpret data.
minors.complements: Statistics strengthens public health, psychology, biology, insurance and economics majors with the methods behind research and analysis.

minors.name: Supply Chain Management
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of purchasing, inventory and logistics.
minors.complements: Supply chain management helps industrial engineering, operations, business and international business majors understand how materials and products move.

minors.name: Sustainability
minors.summary: Adds knowledge of resource use, clean energy and sustainable practices.
minors.complements: Sustainability helps engineering, architecture, HVAC, building science and business majors design and run greener buildings, products and operations.

minors.name: Web Development
minors.summary: Adds the skills to build websites with HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
minors.complements: Web development helps graphic design, marketing and communications majors build the sites they design and promote.
